newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty may take breather after fast rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty may take breather after fast rise.

text.p: The Polish zloty's two-day upward drive against the basket of currencies may take a quick pit-stop on Wednesday as banks take profits on the currency's half percentage point rise since Friday, dealers said.
But they said the Polish currency's upward trend was likely to remain intact as the money market's recent zloty shortage was seen continuing despite a large net cash inflow tomorrow.
"Wednesday may be nervous as banks ponder taking a profit after the zloty's rise, so a correction in the growth trend may occur," said Witold Wozniak of Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
The zloty closed at a six-month high at 2.67/2.63 pct from the trading band centre vs 2.43/2.40 pct on Monday.
It was at 2.8625/33 to the dollar, down from 2.8460/66 on Monday and at 1.8300/10 to the mark, up from 1.8460/66.
Dealers said the zloty's rise was mainly the result of a shortage on the money market as banks searched for zlotys ahead of large anticipated cash ouflows later in December.

They said one-day rates most likely peaked at nearly 24 percent on Tuesday and would slowly inch down for the rest of the week and form around 20-21 percent, still above the central bank's main drainage rate, last at 19.16 percent.

"One-day rates probably peaked on Tuesday after players overinvested in reverse repos last week and, with quick rising credit action and larger December cash ouflows, the demand for zlotys is high," one dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw said.
On Tuesday overnight rates closed at 22.80/23.90 percent, up from Monday's 19.70/20.00, while tomorrow/next finished at 22.50/23.50 percent, up from 19.80/20.00 percent.
